description: This grouped bar chart illustrates the measured "effect" across various language families for four different model configurations. The horizontal axis displays the categorical language groups, ordered partially alphabetically by their "IE-" prefix: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, followed by a category label obscured by a solid grey rectangle, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "effect," using a linear scale with tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at intervals of 10, ranging from 0 to 40. Within each category on the horizontal axis, there is a cluster of four bars representing the model configurations defined in the legend: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green). Every bar features a vertical black error bar extending above and below the top edge, with some lower error bounds extending below the zero line. The light blue mBERT-targ bars generally display the highest values across most categories, reaching the tallest overall height of approximately 35 in the category with the obscured label, and about 28 in the Uralic category. The dark blue XLM-targ bars typically follow as the second tallest, peaking at roughly 26 in the obscured category. The light green mBERT-permute and dark green XLM-permute bars generally show lower values, with the shortest bars found in the Uralic category at approximately 1. A notable exception to this visual trend occurs in the IE-Indic category, where the permute configurations (light and dark green) are taller, at approximately 18 and 16 respectively, while the targ configurations (light and dark blue) are much shorter, at roughly 4 and 5. All bars are visually defined by thin black outlines, and the only specific visual emphasis is the grey rectangle masking one of the horizontal axis labels.
